The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e3240;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; MC	<p>9722_702a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e3240;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e3240;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #686002;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #686002;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686002;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4f681f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #13697a;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #13697a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #13697a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4f681f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #13697a;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #13697a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #13697a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4f681f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4f681f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f681f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #943569;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #943569;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #943569;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e3240;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #686002;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #686002;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686002;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #943569;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #943569;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #943569;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686002;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #686002;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686002;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22658a;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #22658a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22658a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #954122;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #954122;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #954122;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2b6d39;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b6d39;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4d50b5;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4d50b5;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686002;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e46a4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e46a4;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #13697a;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #13697a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #13697a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #853b8c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853b8c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #943569;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #943569;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #943569;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e3240;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3240;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2b5ea3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2b5ea3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686002;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #686002;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686002;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #943569;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #943569;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #943569;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
